# Now 2.13.15
- Full-screen background now matches Apple Music: it's the album artwork itself, heavily blurred and gently enriched, rather than a synthetic color wash. Dark covers now stay genuinely dark (the previous version raised the brightness floor, which washed dark art out with a bright bleed); bright covers stay bright. - Showing/hiding lyrics is now animated: the artwork glides from center to the left as the lyrics rise up from below and settle at the line that's playing; hiding them lets the lyrics fall away as the artwork returns to center. - The glass volume control is now interactive (it reacts under the pointer), and glass elements refract the new, more faithful backdrop.

# Now 2.13.14
- The full-screen view now uses native macOS Liquid Glass (on macOS 26 and later): the close button and the volume control are real glass elements, matching Apple Music. On older macOS they keep the previous translucent look. - Added a lyrics button in the bottom-right corner (glass) to show or hide the lyrics. With lyrics hidden, the view centers the album art and controls.

# Now 2.13.13
- The full-screen background now uses the album art's actual dominant colors, so it matches the cover instead of inventing bright hues. A neutral cover gives a soft neutral wash; a colorful cover gives a vivid one. - The dominant tone fills the whole screen (no dark base), so the backdrop reads brighter and fuller — closer to Apple Music.
